result.description:
Weldworks is hiring a Full-time Construction Project Manager role in West Ryde, NSW. Apply now to be part of our team.

Requirements for this role:

Flexible hours available
2–3 years of relevant work experience required for this role
WELDWORKS PTY LTD is looking for an experienced Construction Project Manager for our client’s construction projects, including residential homes, commercial buildings, civil works and public spaces in Sydney.
On a full-time basis, you will be responsible for planning, organising, directing, controlling and coordinating construction projects, as well as managing the physical, financial and human resources involved in the construction process.

Title: Construction Project Manager, Full-time position
Salary: A$ 90,000.00 to 98,000.00 plus super
Work Location: In person
We are looking for applicants who demonstrate the following:

Requirements
•	Bachelor’s degree or higher in Construction Project Management, Construction Management, Building Technology, Building Science, Civil Engineering or another highly relevant field. 
•	At least 2–3 years of relevant experience managing residential, commercial, industrial or civil construction projects. 
•	Demonstrated experience managing construction schedules, budgets, labour, materials, plant and equipment. 
•	Strong knowledge of construction methods, building legislation, Australian Standards, quality requirements and workplace health and safety procedures. 
•	Ability to read, assess and interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, specifications and construction contracts. 
•	Experience coordinating architects, engineers, consultants, subcontractors, suppliers, tradespeople and relevant authorities. 
•	Strong understanding of tendering, procurement, contract administration and project cost control. 
•	Ability to identify project risks, delays and budget variations and implement appropriate corrective actions. 
•	Strong leadership, communication, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills. 
•	Excellent organisational, reporting and problem-solving abilities. 
•	Current Australian driver licence preferred. 
•	Relevant registration, licence or site accreditation may be required depending on the project and scope of work. 

Construction Project Manager Responsibilities
•	Plan, organise, direct, control and coordinate construction projects from commencement through to completion. 
•	Establish project plans, construction schedules, milestones, budgets and resource requirements. 
•	Interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, technical specifications and contractual requirements. 
•	Determine appropriate construction methods, sequencing, labour requirements, materials, plant and equipment. 
•	Coordinate the procurement and delivery of construction materials, equipment and services. 
•	Consult with architects, engineers, building professionals, consultants, tradespeople and technical workers. 
•	Negotiate and communicate with building owners, property developers, clients, suppliers and subcontractors. 
•	Prepare, review and contribute to tenders, quotations, contract bids and project proposals. 
•	Implement coordinated work programs across construction sites. 
•	Monitor project progress, expenditure, quality, safety, risk and compliance against approved plans and budgets. 
•	Ensure construction activities comply with relevant building legislation, Australian Standards, contractual requirements and workplace health and safety procedures. 
•	Manage and monitor the performance, quality and progress of contractors and subcontractors. 
•	Arrange the submission of plans, permits and supporting documents to relevant authorities. 
•	Coordinate required inspections, approvals and project handover activities. 
•	Prepare progress reports, budget updates, risk assessments and project documentation. 
•	Identify potential delays, cost overruns, quality issues and construction risks and implement appropriate corrective actions. 
•	Lead and supervise site managers, project engineers, supervisors, forepersons, subcontractors and tradespeople as required. 
•	Maintain effective communication with clients and key stakeholders throughout the construction process. 
•	Ensure projects are completed safely, on time, within budget and in accordance with the required quality standards. 

These responsibilities reflect the official ANZSCO functions for Construction Project Managers, including management of construction 
schedules, procurement, contractors, budgets, compliance, inspections and project resources. 
If you would like to discuss the role further, please click APPLY and send through an up-to-date CV. We can schedule a time to discuss the position available and determine whether the role is suitable for your qualifications and experience.
Work Location: In person

Position: 	Office Manager 
Salary: 	       $76,000 – $85,000 Plus Superannuation
Location: 	36 Highlander Dr. Craigieburn VIC 3064
Mode: 		Full-Time
Experience:	1 year experience
Royal 3PL Pty Ltd trading as Northedge Cabinets and Cladding, is an Australian-owned company specialising in the design, manufacture, supply, and installation of premium cabinetry and architectural cladding solutions. The company delivers high-quality products and services to residential, commercial, and multi-unit developments across Australia, working closely with builders, developers, architects, designers, and private clients.
Northedge Cabinets and Cladding provides customised joinery and cabinetry solutions for kitchens, bathrooms, wardrobes, laundries, offices, and other interior spaces, together with innovative cladding systems that enhance the functionality and visual appeal of modern buildings. The company is committed to delivering tailored solutions that meet each client's design requirements while maintaining exceptional standards of workmanship, quality, and customer service.
The business manages projects from initial consultation and design through to manufacturing, project coordination, delivery, and installation. By integrating skilled craftsmanship with efficient project management and modern manufacturing techniques, Northedge Cabinets and Cladding ensures projects are completed on time, within budget, and to the highest industry standards.
As the company continues to expand its operations and undertake an increasing number of residential and commercial projects, it has experienced significant growth in its administrative and operational requirements. This growth has created the need for dedicated management of office operations, customer communications, project administration, supplier coordination, procurement activities, and internal business processes.
To support the continued expansion of the business, Royal 3PL Pty Ltd requires a skilled Office Manager to oversee the company's administrative functions, coordinate office operations, streamline internal processes, and provide essential support to management, production, installation teams, suppliers, and clients. The position plays a critical role in ensuring the efficient day-to-day operation of the business while enabling the company to maintain its high standards of service delivery and support its future growth objectives.
Key Responsibilities:

•	Coordinate the day-to-day administrative operations of the office to ensure efficient workflow and business continuity.
•	Develop, implement and maintain office procedures, administrative systems and record management processes to improve operational efficiency.
•	Coordinate incoming customer enquiries, prepare quotations, maintain job files and ensure project documentation is complete and up to date.
•	Liaise with clients, builders, suppliers and subcontractors regarding project schedules, material deliveries, installation dates and administrative requirements.
•	Prepare and process purchase orders, supplier invoices, customer invoices and related administrative documentation.
•	Monitor office expenditure, maintain financial records and assist management with budget tracking and monthly administrative reports.
•	Coordinate procurement of office supplies and monitor stock of administrative and operational consumables.
•	Maintain accurate records of contracts, supplier agreements, project documentation and company compliance documents.
•	Coordinate staff rosters, leave records, timesheets and other human resources administration activities.
•	Ensure office operations comply with company policies, workplace health and safety procedures and relevant legislative requirements.
•	Prepare regular administrative and operational reports for management to support business planning and decision-making.
•	Identify opportunities to improve office procedures and implement administrative process improvements to enhance productivity and customer service.
•	Provide administrative support to senior management and coordinate communication between office staff, production personnel and installation teams to ensure projects progress efficiently.

ICBM SERVICES PTY LTD is hiring a Full-time Construction Project Manager role across NSW, WA in Australia. Apply now to be part of our team.

Requirements for this role:

Flexible hours available
2–3 years of relevant work experience required for this role
ICBM SERVICES PTY LTD is looking for an experienced Construction Project Manager for our client’s construction projects, including residential homes, commercial buildings, civil works and public spaces in Sydney.
On a full-time basis, you will be responsible for planning, organising, directing, controlling and coordinating construction projects, as well as managing the physical, financial and human resources involved in the construction process.

Title: Construction Project Manager, Full-time position
Salary: A$ 90,000.00 to 98,000.00 plus super
Work Location: In person
We are looking for applicants who demonstrate the following:

Requirements

•	Bachelor’s degree or higher in Construction Project Management, Construction Management, Building Technology, Building Science, Civil Engineering or another highly relevant field. 
•	At least 2–3 years of relevant experience managing residential, commercial, industrial or civil construction projects. 
•	Demonstrated experience managing construction schedules, budgets, labour, materials, plant and equipment. 
•	Strong knowledge of construction methods, building legislation, Australian Standards, quality requirements and workplace health and safety procedures. 
•	Ability to read, assess and interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, specifications and construction contracts. 
•	Experience coordinating architects, engineers, consultants, subcontractors, suppliers, tradespeople and relevant authorities. 
•	Strong understanding of tendering, procurement, contract administration and project cost control. 
•	Ability to identify project risks, delays and budget variations and implement appropriate corrective actions. 
•	Strong leadership, communication, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills. 
•	Excellent organisational, reporting and problem-solving abilities. 
•	Current Australian driver licence preferred. 
•	Relevant registration, licence or site accreditation may be required depending on the project and scope of work. 

Construction Project Manager Responsibilities

•	Plan, organise, direct, control and coordinate construction projects from commencement through to completion. 
•	Establish project plans, construction schedules, milestones, budgets and resource requirements. 
•	Interpret architectural drawings, engineering plans, technical specifications and contractual requirements. 
•	Determine appropriate construction methods, sequencing, labour requirements, materials, plant and equipment. 
•	Coordinate the procurement and delivery of construction materials, equipment and services. 
•	Consult with architects, engineers, building professionals, consultants, tradespeople and technical workers. 
•	Negotiate and communicate with building owners, property developers, clients, suppliers and subcontractors. 
•	Prepare, review and contribute to tenders, quotations, contract bids and project proposals. 
•	Implement coordinated work programs across construction sites. 
•	Monitor project progress, expenditure, quality, safety, risk and compliance against approved plans and budgets. 
•	Ensure construction activities comply with relevant building legislation, Australian Standards, contractual requirements and workplace health and safety procedures. 
•	Manage and monitor the performance, quality and progress of contractors and subcontractors. 
•	Arrange the submission of plans, permits and supporting documents to relevant authorities. 
•	Coordinate required inspections, approvals and project handover activities. 
•	Prepare progress reports, budget updates, risk assessments and project documentation. 
•	Identify potential delays, cost overruns, quality issues and construction risks and implement appropriate corrective actions. 
•	Lead and supervise site managers, project engineers, supervisors, forepersons, subcontractors and tradespeople as required. 
•	Maintain effective communication with clients and key stakeholders throughout the construction process. 
•	Ensure projects are completed safely, on time, within budget and in accordance with the required quality standards. 

These responsibilities reflect the official ANZSCO functions for Construction Project Managers, including management of construction schedules, procurement, contractors, budgets, compliance, inspections and project resources. 
If you would like to discuss the role further, please click APPLY and send through an up-to-date CV. We can schedule a time to discuss the position available and determine whether the role is suitable for your qualifications and experience.

This role suits a methodical and analytical professional with a strong technical background in software and systems testing, a commitment to quality assurance best practices, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, agile environment.
## Key Responsibilities
- Specify, develop, and execute detailed test plans, test scripts, and test cases to validate the behaviour, functionality, and integrity of ICT systems across multiple platforms and environments.
- Identify, diagnose, and document functionality errors and faults in systems and programming code within established testing protocols, quality standards, and compliance guidelines to ensure systems perform to specification.
- Design and conduct regression, integration, performance, and user acceptance testing (UAT) to ensure new and updated systems meet defined requirements and business needs.
- Utilise automated test software and frameworks to streamline testing processes, improve test coverage, and increase efficiency across the software development lifecycle.
- Produce clear and comprehensive defect reports, test summary reports, and related quality assurance documentation, ensuring traceability from requirements through to test outcomes.
- Perform systems architecture reviews and assessments, evaluating current and future hardware and software configurations, and contributing recommendations to inform strategic technical direction.
- Collaborate closely with software developers, business analysts, and project managers to clarify requirements, resolve defects, and support timely delivery of system releases.
- Create, review, and maintain technical documentation including procedural guides, operational manuals, instructional materials, technical specifications, and maintenance inventory records.
- Analyse test results and defect trends to identify recurring issues, recommend process improvements, and support continuous quality improvement initiatives across the organisation.
- Participate in agile ceremonies such as sprint planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives, contributing a quality assurance perspective throughout the development cycle.
- Assess risks associated with system changes and releases, providing input into risk mitigation strategies and supporting informed decision-making across project and operational teams.
- Support the evaluation, selection, and implementation of testing tools, methodologies, and frameworks to ensure the organisation's testing capabilities remain current and effective.
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- A bachelor's degree or higher in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
- Demonstrated experience in ICT systems testing, quality assurance, or a closely related technical role, with a solid understanding of the software development and systems engineering lifecycle.
- Proficiency in writing and executing test plans, test cases, and test scripts across functional, non-functional, and regression testing scenarios.
- Hands-on experience with test automation tools and frameworks such as Selenium, Cypress, JUnit, TestNG, or comparable technologies.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose complex system faults and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Experience producing high-quality technical documentation, including test reports, defect logs, operational guides, and system specifications.
- Familiarity with agile and DevOps methodologies and the ability to integrate quality assurance activities into iterative development workflows.
- Solid understanding of systems architecture, network infrastructure, and software integration concepts relevant to enterprise ICT environments.
- Competency with defect tracking and test management tools such as JIRA, Azure DevOps, Zephyr, or similar platforms.
- Excellent communication, collaboration, and organisational skills, with a strong commitment to delivering quality outcomes within agreed timeframes.
## Preferred Qualifications
- ISTQB certification (Foundation Level or above) or an equivalent recognised qualification in software testing or quality assurance.
- Experience working in regulated industries or environments with strict compliance, security, or governance requirements, such as government, finance, or healthcare.
- Exposure to performance and load testing tools such as Apache JMeter, LoadRunner, or Gatling.
- Familiarity with cybersecurity testing principles, including vulnerability assessments and secure coding practices.
- Experience with cloud-based environments and platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud, and an understanding of how they impact testing strategies.
- Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and associated tools such as Jenkins, GitLab CI, or Bamboo.
- A postgraduate qualification or additional certifications in project management, IT governance, or related fields, such as ITIL or PRINCE2, would be highly regarded.
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a collaborative, inclusive, and forward-thinking team that values technical excellence and continuous improvement, where your contributions directly shape the quality of systems used across the organisation.
- Access ongoing professional development opportunities, including support for industry certifications, training programmes, and attendance at relevant conferences and events.
- Enjoy a flexible working environment with options for hybrid work arrangements, supporting a healthy work-life balance without compromising on career growth.
- Work on complex, large-scale ICT projects that offer genuine variety and the opportunity to deepen your expertise across diverse technologies and industries.
- Receive a competitive remuneration package with a clear pathway for career progression within a growing organisation that invests in its people.
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super
